You would not use a catheter valve when you need accurate hourly urine output (for example, in critically ill or post-operative patients), when the bladder has high pressure, poor compliance, or a risk of reflux to the kidneys, or when the patient cannot sense bladder fullness or operate the valve. The shared note is incorrect: a valve does not measure urine volume, so output must be recorded by draining into a graduated bag.
